;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**[[2017 Temple Mount crisis]]
***The [[Israel]]i government says it will remove metal detectors and some cameras recently installed at the entrances to the [[Temple Mount]] in [[Jerusalem]] that resulted in a wave of protests and some deaths. Instead, less obtrusive surveillance means will be used. [https://www.nytimes.com/2017/07/24/world/middleeast/israel-jordan-aqsa-temple-mount-violence.html (''The New York Times'')] [http://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/1.803266 (''Haaretz'')] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israel-palestinians-idUSKBN1A92Q5 (Reuters)]
*[[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbass]]
**[[Kurt Volker]], U.S. special representative for [[Ukraine]], says in a [[BBC News]] interview that the [[White House]] is considering arming Ukrainian government forces fighting [[Separatist forces of the war in Donbass|Pro-Russian militants]] with defensive weapons. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-40712385 (BBC)]

;Business and economy
*[[Microsoft Paint]]
**Amid a public backlash, [[Microsoft]] reneges on its decision to end its [[Microsoft Paint|Paint]] program and states that it will be placed on its app store rather than bundled with future editions of Windows. [https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/gadgets-and-tech/news/microsoft-paint-dead-windows-coming-back-download-how-to-app-store-3d-a7858536.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[Adobe Flash]]
**[[Adobe Systems]] announces it will stop updating and distributing its multimedia software platform [[Adobe Flash|Flash]] by the end of 2020. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-adobe-systems-flash-idUSKBN1AA22R (Reuters)] [http://money.cnn.com/2017/07/25/technology/adobe-killing-flash/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Jimmy Choo Ltd]]
**[[Michael Kors (brand)|Michael Kors]] buys [[Jimmy Choo Ltd|Jimmy Choo]] for [[United States dollar|US$]]1.2 billion. [https://www.nytimes.com/2017/07/25/business/dealbook/jimmy-choo-michael-kors.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Alternative fuel vehicles]]
**Following a similar move in [[France]], the [[United Kingdom]] is to ban the sale of petrol and diesel cars by [[2040]] in order to reduce [[Air pollution in the United Kingdom|air pollution]]. A new tax will also be levied on diesel car drivers in 2020. [http://news.sky.com/story/petrol-and-diesel-cars-banned-from-uk-roads-by-2040-10962075 (Sky News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*2017 [[heat wave]] in Europe
**Firefighters battle [[wildfire]]s across southern [[France]], including one in [[Corsica]]. [http://www.france24.com/en/20170725-firefighters-struggle-battle-wildfires-across-southern-france-corsica (France 24)]
**[[Pope Francis]] halts the [[fountain]]s of [[Vatican City|The Vatican]] amidst a drought in [[Italy]]. [http://www.cbsnews.com/news/pope-francis-shuts-off-vatican-fountains-in-response-to-rome-italy-drought/ (CBS News)]

;Health and medicine
*[[Chronic traumatic encephalopathy]]
**A study, published in the ''[[JAMA (journal)|Journal of the American Medical Association]]'', finds that 99 percent of the brains donated for scientific research by deceased [[National Football League]] players show signs of [[chronic traumatic encephalopathy]] (CTE), the disease identified in autopsies of numerous NFL players who have committed suicide, and the subject of the 2015 movie ''[[Concussion (2015 film)|Concussion]]''. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-nfl-cte-idUSKBN1AA2BW (Reuters)] [http://www.cnn.com/2017/07/25/health/cte-nfl-players-brains-study/index.html (CNN)] [http://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2645104 (''JAMA'')]

;International relations
*[[Jordan–United States relations]]
**[[Jordan]]ian authorities release a video of a [[Jordanian Air Force]] sergeant shooting [[United States Army|United States soldiers]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2017/07/24/us/video-shows-us-soldiers-surrendering-before-fatal-shooting-in-jordan.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Iran–United States relations]]
**The [[United States Navy]] says the [[USS Thunderbolt|USS ''Thunderbolt'']] fired a warning shot at an [[Iran]]ian patrol boat after it came within 150 yards of the U.S. ship. [http://abcnews.go.com/International/us-navy-ship-fires-multiple-warning-shots-iranian/story?id=48835417 (ABC News)]
*[[United States embargoes]]
**The [[U.S. House of Representatives]] votes in favor of economic sanctions against Russia for its [[Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections|interference in the 2016 U.S. election]], and against [[U.S. sanctions against Iran|Iran]] and [[North Korea–United States relations|North Korea]] for their weapons programs. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/powerpost/house-prepares-to-pass-sanctions-bill--and-set-up-veto-dilemma-for-trump/2017/07/25/ece80164-7138-11e7-8839-ec48ec4cae25_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Efforts to repeal the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act|Efforts to repeal Obamacare]]
**The [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] votes to open debate on repealing and possibly replacing [[Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act|Obamacare]]. [http://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/senate-sets-sights-skinny-repeal-obamacare-tuesday-s-voting-n786296 (NBC News)]
**The Senate votes against the [[American Health Care Act of 2017|Better Care Reconciliation Act of 2017]] amendment. [https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2017/07/25/us/politics/senate-votes-repeal-obamacare.html (''The New York Times'')] 
*Documents that were previously sealed and withheld from the public pertaining to the [[John F. Kennedy assassination]] are released. [https://www.archives.gov/research/jfk/2017-release (U.S. National Archives)]
